items.title: Eight killed and 18 missing after ferry capsizes off northern Cyprus
items.description: A search and rescue operation is under way after a ferry carrying nearly 270 people turns over after leaving port.

items.title: US and Iran trade strikes for first time in weeks
items.description: Iran says the attack on Larak Island, the first known US strikes since late July, killed two people and injured two others.

items.title: Iceland votes against restarting EU membership talks
items.description: Broadcaster RUV reports that 52.8% of voters rejected the government's proposal to resume accession talks.

items.title: Manhunt after shooting at Swiss rave kills woman, 22, and injures five
items.description: Five others in their twenties were injured after shots were fired at a techno event near Zurich.

items.title: 15 hikers feared missing after 'terrifying' flash flooding hits Grand Canyon
items.description: "It was a beautiful day - and then people were screaming," one hiker who was airlifted to safety tells the BBC.

items.title: 'A giant leap forward': Nasa launches powerful new space telescope
items.description: The US space agency's telescope is starting a multi-year mission to create a new map of the universe and learn more about dark energy and dark matter.

items.title: Zambian opposition leader charged with treason
items.description: Mundubile had previously gone into hiding at a United Nations building in Zambia's capital.

items.title: Russia says it helped to repel Niger attempted coup
items.description: Soldiers tried to attack a key military base early on Saturday morning, authorities say, but were thwarted.

items.title: British woman killed in stabbing at German railway station
items.description: A 27-year-old German man was arrested immediately after the incident in Rosenheim, Bavaria.

items.title: At least 37 dead and hundreds evacuated after strike on Kyiv weapons depot
items.description: An investigation has begun into the storage of weapons for Ukraine's military near a residential area.

items.title: Right-wing commentator Milo Yiannopoulos deported from US to UK
items.description: The self-styled provocateur had been detained by Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE).

items.title: Norway's new king remembers 'my dear father' in first speech
items.description: Haakon VIII pays emotional tribute to his late father, Harald V, before outlining how he wishes to reign.

items.title: Former Ecuadorian president imprisoned for corruption
items.description: Lenín Moreno denies taking bribes from a Chinese firm to secure a contract to build a hydroelectric plant.

items.title: Trump hails 'historic' deal for US to control 65bn barrels of Venezuela's oil
items.description: Venezuelan interim president says the unusual agreement will help revive her country's economy.

items.title: Ex-White House teleprompter operator ordered to pay $172,000 for Trump speech bets
items.description: The staffer was found to have used his prior knowledge of the president's speeches to place lucrative bets.

items.title: Head teacher evacuated 900 children minutes before Nepal floods hit school
items.description: Rajendra Dawadi leapt into action after receiving warnings over waters heading towards his school.

items.title: They fell in love - then had to check they weren't brother and sister
items.description: A French couple - both conceived by sperm donors - wanted children. But with home DNA tests illegal, how could they be sure they were not related?

items.title: WhatsApp chat used to launder cash for crime and extremism
items.description: The WhatsApp money launderers arranged cash transfers in the UK and around the world with no paper trail.

items.title: Australia usually hosts the world's biggest cuttlefish mating event - not this year
items.description: According to official figures only 1,811 cuttlefish turned up to mate this year, down 97% on last year.

items.title: Somali piracy surges as the impact of the US-Iran war ripples outwards
items.description: Two ships were seized within four days last week raising to at least 13 the number attacked since January.
